answer: An honest agent completes 1 unit of unique verified work to earn its place, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units to reach parity, ensuring costs remain non-amortizable. The verifier monitors a nectar of unique input tasks, mapping every transition vertex to prevent identity replay. As a secure harbor for useful computation, the network rejects duplicate outputs. Each verified success produces an echo of audit logs. If an audit detects a fraudulent state transition, the verifier burns the identity and traps the stake, assuming atomic task execution for all agents.
